deep.reconstruction:
Context: Gauss–Weber galvanomagnetic experiments in Göttingen, spring 1833. A galvanic circuit ('Galvanische Kette') is passed through a multiplier coil around a suspended magnet read by mirror and scale. The numbers are successive turning points of the swinging magnet, in scale divisions. Each row lists one left and one right turning point, so the time series reads row by row.

The pattern shows the multiplication method (Multiplikationsmethode). The current is reversed at every turning point, so the equilibrium jumps between c+d and c−d. My derivation: if a turning point is x_n and the equilibrium during the next half-swing is e_n, then x_{n+1}=2e_n−x_n. Hence each arc s_n=|x_{n+1}−x_n| grows by 4d per half-swing (ignoring damping). At the mark †/‡ the commutation phase is switched, so the arcs then shrink by about the same amount each half-swing. Gauss's evaluation is: increment per half-swing = (last ascending arc − first arc)/(number of steps), and decrement = (first descending arc − last arc)/(number of steps).

(1) Two plate pairs A, B in series with cloth disks between them.
- Turning points: 644.0, 749.5, 477.0, 905.0, 326.5, 1060.0, 174.5, 1208.5, 24.9†, 1216.5, 171.0, 1060.0, 333.9, 893.0, 501.0, 722.0, 657.5.
- Arcs: 105.5, 272.5, 428, 578.5, 733.5, 885.5, 1034, 1183.6 | 1191.6, 1045.5, 889, 726.1, 559.1, 392, 221, 64.5.
- Ascent: (1183.6−105.5)/7 = 154.0.
- Descent: (1191.6−64.5)/7 = 161.0.
- Mean: 157.5, i.e. the 'beide zusammen 154.0, 161.0 } 157.5' on the page. The struck '76' was a false start.
- My inference: the deflection is d ≈ 157.5/4 ≈ 39.4 divisions.

(2) Plate pair A alone.
- Arcs ascending: 57.6, 134.5, 209, 280, 357, 433.5, 512.3, 585, 661, 735, 813, 892, 971.6, 1051.3, 1130.5, 1209.
- Ascent: (1209−57.6)/15 = 76.76 = 'zuerst 76.76' exactly.
- After ‡ the arcs are 1220, 1171, 1111, 1053, 1000, 951, 903, 853.2, 802.2, 752.1, 701.1, 652, 604, 552.8, 500.8, 454.1, 408.1, 357.2, 305.2, 259, 214.2, 168.2, 121.5, 74.5, 26.9.
- Descent by the same rule: (1220−26.9)/24 = 49.71. Gauss writes 'nachher 51.38'.

(3) Plate pair B alone.
- Turning points: 650.0, 624.0, 699.8, 565.0, 760.0, 504.0, 812.0‡, 501.8, 761.4, 552.5, 713.8, 612.0, 652.2.
- Arcs: 26, 75.8, 134.8, 195, 256, 308 | 310.2, 259.6, 208.9, 161.3, 101.8, 40.2.
- Ascent: (308−26)/5 = 56.40 = 'zuerst'.
- Descent: (310.2−40.2)/5 = 54.00 = 'nachher'.

Interpretation: the labels 'zuerst'/'nachher' (first/afterwards) and the signs of the differences show this is not damping. For B the descent value is smaller than the ascent value, which damping cannot produce. The cell current is weakening in time (polarization), drastically so for A. The single-cell values (≈77+56 at first) are compared with the series combination (157.5).
errors: A alone, 'nachher 51.38': recomputing with the method that reproduces all his other figures exactly gives (1220.0−26.9)/24 = 49.71, not 51.38. No natural choice of endpoints or step count from the transcribed readings yields 51.38. This is either an arithmetic slip or a different selection of data. The individual decrements scatter between about 45 and 60, so the discrepancy is within that scatter but not explained by it.
The A,B combined values (154.0, 161.0, 157.5), A ascent (76.76) and B ascent/descent (56.40, 54.00) all check exactly.

results.what: Measurement of galvanic current strength by the multiplication method: reversing the current at each turning point of a magnetometer needle and taking the mean growth of the arc per half-swing (≈4× the static deflection).
results.modern_name: Multiplication (ballistic resonance) method of galvanometry / Gauss–Weber multiplication method
results.usually_credited_to: Gauss and W. Weber (1830s; described in the 'Resultate aus den Beobachtungen des magnetischen Vereins', 1837–38)

results.what: Combining the ascending and descending phases (switching the commutation phase at maximum) and averaging, to cancel damping or drift effects; detection of time decay (polarization) of single cells.
results.modern_name: Symmetric up/down averaging to eliminate systematic effects; observation of cell polarization

deep.surprise_reason: These are routine laboratory data from the well-documented Gauss–Weber galvanomagnetic program of 1833, evaluated with their known multiplication method. There is no new mathematics. At most it is a dated instance of the method in use, plus one apparent arithmetic slip.

checkable.asserts: Ascent increment per half-swing for A,B combined ≈ 154.0
A alone ascent = 76.76 exactly as written
A alone descent by same rule = 49.71, not Gauss's 51.38
Implied static deflection for A,B combined ≈ 39.4 scale divisions (arc grows by 4d per half-swing)

transcription_corrections: 'Plattenp.[?] A allein' – reads 'Plattenp. A allein' (abbreviation of Plattenpaar); no doubt needed.
In 'Also beide zusammen' the struck-through '76' is a false start (probably of 76.76) before the bracketed values 154.0 / 161.0 } 157.5.
Marks after 24.9, 28.0 and 812.0 are the commutation-phase switch marks (†/‡), not digits.
